content.title: How rare is it for a Final Four team to not make the next year’s NCAA tournament?
content.text: Auburn BasketballUpdated: Mar. 15, 2026, 8:39 p.m.Published: Mar. 15, 2026, 5:54 p.m.By Creg Stephenson | cstephenson@al.comAuburn’s slide from a Final Four team in 2025 to out of the NCAA tournament entirely is not only not unprecedented; it’s not even all that rare.The Tigers (17-16) failed to earn a spot in March Madness this season and will instead play in the NIT. Auburn hosts South Alabama in a first-round game on Tuesday night (9 p.m., ESPN2). Auburn became the 10th team in just the last decade to fail to make the NCAA tournament a year after reaching the Final Four. Most recent was North Carolina State last year, which slipped all the way to 12-19 and no postseason berth of any kind in 2025.Here’s the full list: YearSchoolRecordPost?2026Auburn17-16NIT2025NC State12-19None2024Miami, Fla.15-17None2023North Carolina20-13None 2023Villanova17-17NIT2019Loyola (Ill.)20-14NIT2018Oregon23-13NIT2018South Carolina17-16NIT 2017Oklahoma11-20None2017Syracuse19-15NIT Since the NCAA tournament expanded to 64 teams in 1985, five SEC teams have failed to reach March Madness a year after making the Final Four. The previous four were the aforementioned 2018 South Carolina team, along with Florida in 2015 and 2008 (the latter when the Gators were two-time defending NCAA champions) and 1997 Mississippi State.Here’s that list: YearSchoolRecordPost?2026Auburn17-16NIT2018South Carolina17-16None2015Florida16-17None2008Florida*24-12NIT1997Mississippi State12-18None * — defending NCAA champion The NCAA began allowing more than one team from each conference to make the tournament in 1975. Auburn this year is the ninth SEC team in that span that failed to make the tournament a year after reaching the Final Four. That list includes another defending champion, Kentucky in 1979.
